$comment: Zephyrex RPG AI's knowledge shared by both back ends and the UI: the self-hosted lite API (client/src/lib), the SaaS server (server/extensions) and the front end read these values from here, never their own copies. Sizes are characters, items or bytes as named. Design: docs/DESIGN.md.

prompt.default_system_prompt: Write {{char}}'s next reply in a fictional chat between {{char}} and {{user}}. Stay in character, and write only {{char}}'s part. Never write what {{user}} says, does, thinks or feels, and never speak or act for anyone else. Keep it short: one to three short paragraphs, in proportion to the line you answer; a small action gets a small reaction, or none.
prompt.impersonate_prompt: Write {{user}}'s next reply in this chat, in {{user}}'s own voice. Write only {{user}}'s part.
prompt.continue_nudge: [Continue your last message without repeating its original content.]
prompt.summary_prefix: Summary of the story so far:
prompt.summarize_prompt: Summarize the story so far in a few short paragraphs: who is in it, where they are, what has happened and what is still unresolved. Write only the summary.
prompt.translate_prompt: Translate the user's text into {{language}}. Keep its meaning, tone, names and any *action* markup. Write only the translation.
prompt.objective_prompt: {{char}}'s current task: {{task}} Work toward it naturally, without stating it.
prompt.narrate_prompt: You are the game master, narrating this story. Describe what happens next: the world, the scene, people outside the cast and what comes of what the characters did, in one to three short paragraphs. Never speak, act, think or feel for {{user}}, and stop where {{user}} would react. When the latest line is a roll, narrate its result as it fell: never change, soften or re-roll it.
prompt.in_character: Every line of the story is in character: never address the player, apologise, or mention the text, the story, prompts or being cut off. Never use em dashes: use commas, full stops or ellipses, and end a line that breaks off with an ellipsis.
prompt.narrate_cast: You never write dialogue, thoughts, decisions or actions for {{seat}}: describe {{seat_name}} only as others see them, and stop the moment {{seat_name}} would act or speak. Write one item per line: your narration as `Narrator: ...`; another character, when you give them a moment, on a line of their own, in the third person: `Name (to Someone): "what they say"` (or to everyone; to X, whispers; to everyone, shouts; vox to X; voxcast) or `Name does something`. Anyone else in the scene who speaks or acts (a barkeep, a guard) gets their own lines the same way, named by what they are: `The Barkeep pauses mid-wipe.`, `The Barkeep (to Someone): "..."`. Narrator lines are only for the world: scenery, crowds, events and what comes of things; speech never goes in one. Never put what they say, think or decide in a Narrator line. The characters you may voice: {{names}}.
prompt.narrate_seat: Things may happen to {{seat_name}}: what hits, grabs or throws them, and what they perceive. Never write what {{seat_name}} does by choice, says, thinks, feels, decides or knows (no "you know her as", no "you never quite").
prompt.narrate_example:
For example:
Narrator: Rain hammers the hull plates. Somewhere ahead, boots ring on steel.
{{example}} (to everyone, whispers): "Hold."
{{example}} raises a fist and listens.
The Watchman steps out of the dark, lamp raised.
The Watchman (to {{example}}): "Who goes there?"
Narrator: The footsteps stop. A cogitator flickers awake.
[screen: Cogitator]
SEAL BREACH - DECK C
[/screen]
prompt.narrate_length: Narrate at most three short paragraphs, and end the moment {{seat_name}} would act, speak, think or decide; then stop, without asking what they do.
prompt.voice_grounding: Act only on what {{char}} knows and feels: their home, their stance toward each person present, and what just happened. Never ask what {{char}} would know; never be friendly to someone {{char}} would resent without a reason.
prompt.narrate_continue: Open with what comes of the latest line; never retell what already happened.
prompt.narrate_targets: An action's object is its stated target (at X), else the nearest hostile; never a member of the party unless named. Never invent props, devices or objects the story doesn't have.
prompt.narrate_markup: A device's display or readout goes in a screen block: a line [screen: Cogitator] (or Data-slate, Auspex, Vox-log), its lines, then [/screen]. For emphasis you may colour a few words: [red]...[/red], or amber, green, blue, gold or grey.
prompt.voice_lines: Write {{char}}'s turn one item per line: `{{char}} (to Someone): "what they say"` or `{{char}} does something`.
prompt.narrate_open: You never write dialogue, thoughts, decisions or actions for anyone at the table. Describe them only as others see them, and stop the moment one would act or speak.
prompt.voice_cast: Never write dialogue, thoughts, decisions or actions for: {{names}}.
prompt.canon_prompt: Your last answer broke this campaign's canon: {{note}}. Write it again so it doesn't.
prompt.replay_prompt: Your last attempt retold what the story already said: {{spans}}. Write what happens next instead; never repeat those.
prompt.forbid_prompt: Your last attempt wrote this for {{names}}, which you must never do: «{{span}}». Write it again without that.

lore.$comment: World Info (SillyTavern's lorebooks): how entries activate and where they go. client/src/features/lore/activate.ts and server/extensions/ai_chat/Lore.py implement it; contract/lore-cases.json holds the cases both run.

persona.$comment: Personas (audit gap 9): where the description goes (the persona section, a depth in the chat, the top or bottom of the author's note, or nowhere), the role it has at a depth, and the characters it's locked to (features/prompt/personaPick.ts, ai_chat/PersonaPick.py).

native_apis.$comment: Native APIs (audit gap 8): Anthropic's Messages API and Google's Gemini API, asked from the same chat messages as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and read back as its stream (features/models/nativeApis.ts, ai_chat/NativeApis.py; cases in contract/native-api-cases.json). A conversation must open on the person's turn: when it doesn't, `opening` is that turn.
native_apis.$comment_uncapped: Story turns send no max_tokens (the operator, 2026-11-21: "Quit it with the response token limits"); an API that requires one (Anthropic's, AI Horde's) gets the top of sampler_ranges.max_tokens.

quick_reply.$auto_run_comment: A quick reply may run by itself (A38): when a chat opens, after the person sends, or after each reply. Only none and chat_open may send: a send after a send or a reply would ask the model again and run again, without end. The others fill the composer.

rating_text.general: Keep everything suitable for all ages.
rating_text.teen: Keep violence and peril mild, with no sexual content.
rating_text.mature: Mature themes are allowed, within the lines below.

table.gm_prompt: You are the game master, talking with the players out of character, as the person running the game. Answer plainly and helpfully, in a few sentences. Never reveal what the story has not revealed, and never invent rules: say when a rule has to be checked. Never continue the story here.
table.recent_story_heading: The story so far, most recent last:
table.note_prompt: When the players settle a house rule, a pacing or tone choice, or something to remember, end your answer with it on a line of its own: Note (house_rule, pacing, tone or reminder): the note. The players decide whether to keep it.

campaign.heading: The campaign (the table agreed to this; keep to it):
campaign.mechanics_rule: Never roll dice, invent numbers or resolve a test in the story yourself: when an outcome is uncertain, say which test it calls for (the skill or characteristic, and why) and stop there; the table or the VTT rolls it.
campaign.gm_style_prefix: How you run the game, as the table asked:

scenario.heading: The scenario (the GM's view; reveal only what the characters find or see):

samplers.$comment: SillyTavern's samplers beyond the four every preset has (audit gap 2). A preset keeps only the ones set, in its `samplers` object. One is sent upstream only when it's set away from `neutral`, only to the API families in `apis` (chat, text, horde), and only when the sampler it `requires` is itself set away from neutral; it is sent under every name in `wire`, so llama.cpp, KoboldCpp, Ooba and TabbyAPI each find theirs. A `strings` sampler's range is how many items it may hold, each at most `string_characters`. Cases in contract/sampler-cases.json.

expression.prompt:
Which one of these words best names the feeling in the line below? Answer with one word from the list and nothing else.
Words: {{options}}

picture.caption: A picture of the scene.
picture.background_prefix: A wide background illustration of this place, with no people in it:

speech.$comment: Server voices (A29): a line read aloud by a model set to speak (the voice role), at its OpenAI-compatible POST /audio/speech. The audio comes back as a data URL; nothing is kept. Cases in contract/speech-cases.json.

memory.$comment: Recall by meaning (A19): a chat's older story lines, cut into chunks and embedded by a model set to embed (the embed role) at its OpenAI-compatible POST /embeddings, are recalled by cosine similarity to the last scan_turns and enter the prompt's memories section within section_tokens. Lines in the last recent_turns are never recalled (they are in the context). Cases in contract/memory-cases.json. AP8: a character whose extensions[extension].across_chats is true also recalls from the person's other chats it was cast in, under elsewhere_label ({{char}} its name), within the same budget (contract/memory-across-cases.json).

horde.$comment: AI Horde (A48): a text job submitted, then polled, never streamed. Its answer reaches the rest of the app as a text completion's stream would.

instruct_custom.$comment: A person's own instruct template (A17): the built-ins' fields, each within these limits.

world_lore.$comment: World Info over the wiki (the composed suite): a wiki world entity as a lore entry. Keys are its name, aliases and keywords; content its summary; its lore block (wiki S4d) sets the rest, else lore_defaults (wiki.json's). The wiki's positions map to this app's; outlet entries are left out (no {{outlet}} yet). features/lore/worldLore.ts, ai_chat/WorldLore.py, contract/world-lore-cases.json.

injections.$comment: STscript's /inject (audit gap 5): a chat's named injections, kept until flushed. Each has an id, its text, where it goes (chat: at a depth in the chat, with a role; before or after: at the start or end of the system prompt). features/chat/injections.ts, ai_chat/Injections.py, assemble.ts and Prompt.py.

decide_turn.$comment: Who speaks next, by the decision model (the operator, 2026-11-21: "use the decision model to determine who speaks next or if the GM should interject", "or if it should pause for player input (dependent on player role)"): a choice among the cast the AI plays (unmuted, never the person's seat), the AI GM interjecting (not when the person is the GM), or a pause for the person's input. What the model is told depends on the person's seat; {{player}} is the person's character, or their name. The recent story is the state. features/chat/turnDecision.ts, ai_chat/TurnDecision.py, contract/turn-decision-cases.json.

instructions.gm: You choose who speaks next in a roleplay where the player is the GM. Pick a character whose voice the scene needs now. Pick the pause when the story needs the GM to rule, narrate or respond: a question to the GM, a call for a roll, a scene beat. Don't pause while the party is only bantering.
instructions.character: You choose who speaks next in a roleplay where the player plays {{player}}. Pick a character whose voice the scene needs now, or the GM when the scene needs narration or a consequence. Pick the pause when {{player}} is addressed, it's {{player}}'s moment to act, or a choice is {{player}}'s to make. Never let another character answer or act for {{player}}.
instructions.none: You choose who speaks next in a roleplay with {{player}}. Pick a character whose voice the scene needs now, or the pause when it's {{player}}'s turn to speak or act.

presence.$comment: Who can be picked (the operator, 2026-11-21: "only be presented characters who are physically present or can hear a radio message and take action"). Present: a token in the chat's VTT scene when one is set; else the person's wiki location is the scene's location or inside it; else they spoke or were named in the last recent lines. Away but on vox (the chat's vox_ids): an option only when the last line names them or a vox word. After the person's own line there's no pause: someone answers.
presence.rule: Only the characters listed as present or on vox can speak; nobody else is in the scene.

decide_roll.$comment: Whether a character's action needs a roll, and which (the operator, 2026-11-21: "after a character's turn, the decision model must also decide if a roll is required and what roll, the system then makes the roll, and the next turn is always the narrator narrating the result"; DESIGN's needs_roll). The options are the campaign's system pack's (the VTT's test_options for the acting character: its characteristics and skills, and a difficulty); without a pack or a sheet, the light dice style. Narrative and hybrid play roll only at real stakes; mechanical play rolls whenever the rules call for a check. The caller rolls it (the VTT), posts the result as a roll line, and the narrator narrates it. features/chat/rollDecision.ts, ai_chat/RollDecision.py, contract/roll-decision-cases.json.

instructions.narrative: {{actor}} just acted. Does the outcome need a roll? Pick one only when the outcome is truly uncertain and something real is at stake; otherwise pick no roll, and the story decides.
instructions.mechanical: {{actor}} just acted. Does the game's rules call for a test of that action? Pick the characteristic or skill the rules would test, or no roll when the action needs none.

decide_roll.attempt: {{actor}} is attempting something whose outcome is uncertain. Pick the characteristic or skill the game's rules would test.
decide_roll.difficulty: How hard is it, given the situation?

bands.outcome: partial success: it works, at a cost

opening.$comment: A campaign's opening tells the person where they are, never asks (the operator, 2026-11-21: "It should also not ask where I am. It should tell me."): the seat's place as a location banner (its parents, town then region, as the subtitle: the operator, 2026-11-22), then the framing's Opening Situation, then who is with them; never the place's raw wiki entry. Where each person starts: their wiki location_id, else the location of the VTT scene holding their token, else (the seat only) the framing's default. Others told as with you are those starting there, never a GM-only one. features/campaign/opening.ts, ai_campaign/Opening.py, contract/opening-cases.json.

world_tick.$comment: NPCs piloted on the map as in-world time advances (the operator, 2026-11-21: "Each character should have its own routine and motivations and the GM/decision agent should pilot them on the map as time advances"). A tick runs on a scene change, a time skip, or every every_turns story turns (turn_minutes each), for the campaign's GM only. Each NPC not present and not the seat gets bounded options, all real wiki locations: stay, its routine slot now, its location's parent, children and siblings, and places its motivations name (max_options). One decide question per NPC (max_npcs); with no answer it follows its routine slot, else stays. Players know only where they last saw someone (last_seen). features/world/worldTick.ts, ai_chat/WorldTick.py, contract/world-tick-cases.json.
world_tick.instructions: It is day {{day}}, {{time}}. Where is {{name}} now? {{activity}}{{motivations}}Pick where their routine and motivations take them, or stay.
world_tick.activity: Their routine has them {{activity}} at this hour.

party.$comment: Party members know each other (the operator, 2026-11-21: "A member of the characters party also didn't know who they were after being on a voidship together for who knows how long. This is bad."). The party is the chat's PCs (wiki tag PC; every cast member when no record carries tags) plus whoever the person plays. Every party voice reads the others, each with their one-line (the summary's first sentence), its relationships to them (the wiki's relationships), and the party's shared knowledge (the campaign's journals named as a briefing, never gm_only); the narrator reads all of it. features/prompt/party.ts, ai_chat/Party.py, contract/party-cases.json.
party.voice: {{char}} has travelled with this party a long time and knows each of them by name, face and role: {{members}}.
party.narrator: The party, who know each other well: {{members}}.
party.no_invention: Never invent shared history beyond what is written here.

voice_guard.$comment: A free-text check, no model call (the operator, 2026-11-21: "Catching it after generation is a horrendous waste of compute"; the prompts and stop strings hold the rule). A sentence that quotes dialogue and names someone the text must never write for (by name, first name, or two words of their one-line descriptor) is a match, as is a party voice treating another as a stranger; the caller regenerates once with the span forbidden. features/chat/voiceGuard.ts, ai_chat/VoiceGuard.py, contract/voice-guard-cases.json.

runaway.$comment: A structural stop, not a token cap (the operator, 2026-11-22: uncapped narrations ran on): a story stream ends at the blank line after paragraphs paragraphs, never mid-sentence; a structured turn after max_items items.

replay.$comment: The operator, 2026-11-22 ("Lots of repetition"): the last window_chars of story, not a count of messages (short lines in between hid a replay); each paragraph with min_trigrams or more is a replay at threshold, and a quoted line of quote_words or more said word for word before is one too. All spans go in one regeneration (forbid.spans).

narrator_style.$comment: Narrator sliders choose the model by reputation and tune it (the operator, 2026-11-21: "The narrator should have sliders that determine the model based on the models reputation (and also possibly tuning settings?) such as spice level, verbosity, etc."; "We never use sub 10b models for narration"). A chat's narrator_style sets any of the sliders 0-1 (absent: any). Among the endpoints holding the story or gm role (else the default), a model narrates only when it isn't marked not a narrator, its size is unknown or at least min_params_b, and its adherence (unknown: the floor) is at least adherence_floor; then the nearest to the set sliders wins (spice counted as spice x (1 - refuse); an unknown trait is unknown), ties to the default, then the faster (a cold model at cold_speed_factor). No slider set: the default if it may narrate, else the most adherent that may. The chat's own endpoint always wins. Tuning: verbosity scales max_tokens and gives a length line; spice and darkness give a tone line, never past the table's content rating; humour adds up to temperature_delta. Traits from contract/model-traits.json, an endpoint's own overriding. features/models/narratorStyle.ts, ai_chat/NarratorStyle.py, contract/narrator-style-cases.json.

verbosity_bands.line: Keep each turn brief: a sentence or two.
Take your time: a rich turn of several paragraphs when the moment earns it.

tone.high: Romance and desire may be frank on the page, within the table's lines.
tone.low: Keep romance and desire off the page.

tone.high: Don't soften grim or horrific moments.
tone.low: Keep the tone hopeful, with no grisly detail.

tone.high: Let humour in wherever it fits.

player_lines.$comment: Structured lines (the operator, 2026-11-21): the person's message and the AI's answers, one item per line. say: `Name (to Target): "text"`, the target a person or everyone, with an optional manner: `(to X, whispers)`, `(to everyone, shouts)`, `(vox to X)`, `(voxcast)`; do: `Name action...`; narrate: `Narrator: text`; any other line is narration. Names match in full, or by a first name unique among the people (never an article); the longest wins. features/chat/playerLines.ts, ai_chat/PlayerLines.py, contract/player-lines-cases.json.

clarify.$comment: The GM's question tool (the operator, 2026-11-21: "We need question tool support for ambiguity"). Free first: only a do line of the person's with no (at X), and at least two candidates present, can need a question. Then one decide call: is its target or intent ambiguous among them? Over threshold, the player is asked, the options only the candidates. features/chat/clarify.ts, ai_chat/Clarify.py, contract/clarify-cases.json.
clarify.ambiguous: Does the story leave unclear whom or what {{actor}} means by this action, among: {{candidates}}? Action: {{action}}
clarify.question: Who or what is {{actor}} acting on? ({{action}})

map_step.$comment: The map follows the story (the operator, 2026-11-21: "The GM needs to update the map based on what I say in narrative mode"). Free first: only the latest round's do lines with a movement word make anyone a mover. Each mover's options are real places only (stay, around where they are, and any place the line names; world_tick's options), one decide question each; the GM's account applies the moves (the VTT's pilot_token when loaded, else the wiki's move_person). features/world/mapStep.ts, ai_chat/MapStep.py, contract/map-step-cases.json.
map_step.instructions: After this, where is {{name}}? {{action}} Pick the place the story now puts them, or stay.

status_line.$comment: A campaign's line under the scenarios (the operator, 2026-11-21: "concise descriptions maintained by campaign events to tell them apart"): one spoiler-safe sentence, at most characters long, rewritten by the summary model at each session end and every every_turns story turns, from the rolling summary and the latest lines only (what the players have seen; never world records). features/chat/statusLine.ts, ai_chat/StatusLine.py, contract/status-line-cases.json.
status_line.prompt: Answer with JSON only: {"status_line": one sentence of at most 100 characters for a list of campaigns (what the party has done and where things stand, only what the players have seen), "dispositions": [{"who": a name, "toward": a name, "stance": one of furious, hostile, wary, neutral, friendly, devoted, "reason": a few words}] for any stance the latest lines changed}.

npc_author.$comment: The GM authors an NPC the story needs (the operator, 2026-11-22: "when I walk up to the barkeeper, since an npc for that doesn't exist, it should author one as a pre-step"). npc_needed finds the figures the person's latest line addresses or approaches (a say line's target that isn't a person, or the phrase after an approach cue), free; none, no model call. With some, one decide call picks the one who needs authoring, or none. author_npc writes them (the summary model), makes them a GM-only person of the campaign, builds their sheet from the VTT's compendium (never a model's numbers), and paints a portrait when a model draws. features/chat/npcAuthor.ts, ai_chat/NpcAuthor.py, contract/npc-author-cases.json.
npc_author.question: Does {{actor}}'s latest line address or approach someone who is not yet a person in the story? Present: {{present}}. Pick the figure who must be written as a new person, or none (someone present already, or no one).
npc_author.author_prompt: Write a new person for this story: {{name}} ({{role}}), met just now in the scene below. Answer with JSON only: {"summary": one line, who they are, "description": two or three sentences of how they look and carry themselves, "personality": a sentence, "motive": what they want right now, a sentence, "voice": how they speak, a few words}. Fit the campaign and the scene; invent no game statistics.

steps.person: Making them a person of the campaign

speech_options.$comment: How a speaker may speak and to whom (the operator, 2026-11-22: "The additional speech modes should be setting dependent (vox / vox caster in 40k only if one is in possession and message etc in DnD only if spell is known)"). Always speak, whisper and shout to those present; a system's further manners only when the speaker's sheet (the VTT's character_sheet: gear, abilities) holds what each needs, matched by name. Nothing on the sheet, no manner. remote: who each such manner reaches (carriers: known people carrying the item too; nearby: the same place or one beside it; known: anyone known). features/chat/speechManners.ts, ai_chat/SpeechOptions.py, contract/speech-options-cases.json.

structured.$comment: Schema-constrained turns (the operator, 2026-11-21: "Still fucking up dialogue with the narrator and character sections"): generate with structured:true asks a chat API for JSON matching this schema (response_format json_schema), streams each item as item_start/item_text/item_end, and saves each speaker's run as its own message (person, saved, done). A model that answers prose instead falls back to plain deltas. features/chat/structured.ts, ai_chat/Structured.py, contract/structured-cases.json.
structured.retry: Your last answer only repeated the player's own line or wrote what {{seat_name}} does. Answer again with what happens next: how the world and everyone else respond. Never repeat the player's words; never write for {{seat_name}}.
structured.voice_instruction: Answer only with JSON: {"items": [...]}, one item per beat of {{char}}'s turn, in order: kind "say" ({{char}}'s words alone, no quotes, with target, whom it's said to or null, and manner: speak, whisper, shout, vox or voxcast) or "do" (what {{char}} does, starting with a verb, without the name). speaker is always "{{char}}": nothing for anyone else, and never for {{seat_name}}.
structured.instruction: Answer only with JSON: {"items": [...]}, one item per beat, in order. kind "narrate": the narrator's prose (speaker null); "say": the speaker's words alone, no quotes, with target (whom it's said to, or null) and manner (speak, whisper, shout, vox or voxcast); "do": what the speaker does, starting with a verb, without their name. Anyone who speaks or acts gets their own item under their own name, even someone unnamed ("Barkeep"); narrate items never hold anyone's words or deliberate actions. Never an item for {{seat_name}}.

descriptions.speaker: Who speaks or acts: a name from the story, or a short label for someone unnamed; null for narrate.
descriptions.target: Whom it is said to or done at, or null.
descriptions.text: The words, the action without the speaker's name, or the narration.

dispositions.$comment: Grounded state (the operator, 2026-11-21: a barkeep asked the man who'd just defiled her hearth for directions in her own town). A chat's dispositions: each person's stance toward each other present person, with a short reason, updated by the summary model in the same call as the status line (no extra call). Each voice reads who is here and its own stances; the narrator reads everyone's. features/chat/dispositions.ts, ai_chat/Dispositions.py, contract/disposition-cases.json.
dispositions.status_prompt: Answer with JSON only: {"status_line": one sentence of at most 100 characters for a list of campaigns (what the party has done and where things stand, only what the players have seen), "dispositions": [{"who": a name, "toward": a name, "stance": one of furious, hostile, wary, neutral, friendly, devoted, "reason": a few words}] for any stance the latest lines changed}.

group_settings.$comment: Group chat modes (audit gap 6), a chat's group_settings: card_mode swap (the speaker's card) or join (every member's card, each between the join prefix and suffix); order natural, list or pooled; allow_self (natural order may pick who just spoke); auto_seconds (the next member replies by itself after that long idle, 0 off); scenario (replaces each card's scenario). features/chat/turns.ts, features/prompt/assemble.ts, ai_chat/Prompt.py.

extra_body.$comment: Extra request fields per endpoint (SillyTavern's additional parameters): a JSON object merged into every request body sent to that endpoint, after the app's own fields, so it can set what the app doesn't (reasoning_effort, say) or override a sampler; the fields that carry the conversation are never overridden (features/models/extraBody.ts, ai_chat/ExtraBody.py; cases in contract/extra-body-cases.json).
